claims.statement: Funder Match is judged entirely in code under match-v2 (RUBRIC_VERSION) with seven weighted criteria: theme 25, geography 15, population 15, eligibility 20, relationship 10, funding size 10, capacity 5. rubric.py counts and is pure, while rules.py judges, so rule changes go in rules.py and point values or tiers go in rubric.py. matching/CLAUDE.md is a short pointer that sends facts to the wiki page, rules and decisions to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §5, and asks for make wiki-update after a change.

Scoring arithmetic: unknown criteria (points None) are excluded from both earned and judged_max rather than counted as zero. A pair sharing no place or theme (neither theme nor geography earned points) gets no score. Tiers are strong at 75 or more, medium at 55 or more, otherwise weak, and not_scored when there is no score. Status (met at 80% of max, partial, fail, unknown) is computed from points.

Criterion and Match validation enforce evidence discipline: points must lie within 0..max, a judged criterion must cite the rows it rests on (except a zero relationship), and a Match must contain every rubric criterion once in rubric order. Match score and tier are computed from the criteria.

Theme is judged on the finest grain both sides share (theme or sub-theme 25, Schedule VII clause 15, domain 10), with domain-others excluded from the domain grain. Points are capped at 15 when no programme carries the shared grain, and the finding comes with an improvement action.

Geography scores a shared district 15, shared state 12 (a district's state is its parent), funder gives across India 6, and a funder region containing an org state 6. It scores 0 when both sides have places and none match, and unknown when a side has none or when a funder region has no recorded member states.

Eligibility is the share of counted items held (12A, 80G, audited accounts, and CSR Form 1 only for corporate_csr/corporate_foundation or Section 135 funders) times 20. Lapsed or missing items earn nothing, while conflicting rows or an unreadable registry are left out of the count and reported in not_judged. The funder's own free-text bars are listed for human review and never scored.

Relationship, funding size and capacity: relationship gives 10 for a confirmed partner line, 5 if unconfirmed, and 0 otherwise. Funding size needs a funder range plus org income (smallest grant at or below income gets 10, up to 2x gets 5, otherwise 0). Capacity looks at spend in the last three completed Indian fiscal years (April start): 5 for all, 3 for some, unknown for none.

match.py builds the card (up to two fit and two gap lines, or a single 'No shared place or theme recorded' line when unscored), the summary and the improve list from templates; improve is empty for unscored matches and not_judged includes unknown criteria.

repositories/matching.load reads the org, funders (all when funder_ids is None, using one fixed query plan) and locations in a single read-only transaction with a statement timeout. It builds themes from the tag taxonomy (domain, theme, sub_theme, csr_sector) so each tag brings its ancestors and Schedule VII clauses, and it never reads Darpan sector tags. Funder themes include the classifications of its activity lines, and registered locations are kept apart from where it gives.

matching.may_run permits staff or an admin or steward of the org, mirroring the 0042 insert rule. It is used by compare_fit, while REST uses the find_org may_run flag from the same RLS functions (app.my_match_org_ids() or app.is_staff()).

service.run_and_save reads profiles with a reader pool (the owner, so every runner judges the same inputs) and writes with a writer pool under that writer's RLS, one run_id per call, returning a tier count. rows() converts each match to a funder_matches row (NULL score when unscored, card JSON) plus a funder_match_details payload, with empty criteria and not_judged for unscored matches.

insert_run writes all rows of a run (match plus detail) in one transaction after taking pg_advisory_xact_lock(4104, org_id), so one run per org is written at a time. All rows share the transaction's now() as run_at, and reruns add new rows and never edit old ones.

Migration 0042 makes saved runs append-only: authenticated has only SELECT and INSERT on funder_matches and funder_match_details, with RLS enabled. Read requires org membership or staff, with detail rows following their match. Insert requires app.my_match_org_ids() (admin or steward of the org) or staff, with run_by equal to app.user_id(). Detail insert is allowed only beside a match the caller wrote. run_by is NULL for make match.

REST routes under /funder-matches: GET ?org= returns the latest run ranked with tier counts and prev_score from the previous run, and 404s an org the caller cannot read. GET /{id}/detail returns one match's reasoning. POST /runs?org= returns 201 and 403s a caller who may read but not run, and calls run_and_save with the owner pool as reader and the caller pool as writer.

The Ask tool compare_fit refuses before reading any data when the chat user may not run a match for the org. Otherwise it loads via repositories/matching, compare() judges each funder, and render() returns plain text, one fact per line (header with tier counts and unknown-criteria counts, then funders), rather than JSON, so an evicted oversized reply still pages. With funder_ids omitted it is a shortlist: only scored funders are listed, the top strong/medium fits (up to FULL_DETAIL_MAX=10) in full without summary and the rest as one-liners, and unscored funders are split into 'nothing in common recorded' (a real non-fit) versus 'the funder has nothing recorded' (unknown, no places or themes). With funder_ids every named funder is in full with its summary. Errors are returned as 'compare_fit failed' strings rather than raised, and ask/agent.py lists it in TOOLS as the one commented exception to the agent's discover-then-db_query access to the database.
make match runs python -m app.matching.run, which saves a run for every org or one (by slug or id), as the owner pool with run_by NULL, and prints funders checked and tier counts.

The Funder Match UI fetches the latest run from /api/funder-matches (FunderMatchView), ranks strong and medium matches while folding weak and not-scored ones into a disclosure shown only at the default view (no bucket, type, proposal filter or search), offers a Rerun (shown only when the list's may_run is true) that POSTs a run and reloads the list. Each MatchCard shows tier, score and a delta against prev_score (only when both exist and differ), and lazy-loads its per-match detail from /api/funder-matches/{id}/detail the first time 'Why this score' is opened.

match-v2 (2026-10-11) changed only the theme criterion and the rubric version: theme now compares the taxonomy tree rather than Darpan sector tags, Others never counts as a shared area, and older saved runs keep their stored rubric_version.

A proposal starts only from a match card: ProposalAction (shown with the Start button only when the list's may_run is true) posts {org, funder_id, title} via startProposal to POST /api/proposals, refreshes the shared proposals store, and navigates into the new proposal through AskWorkspace's openProposals URL params. Members who may not run only see View/count actions.

POST /proposals gates creation: 404 when the caller cannot read the org, 403 when they can read but not run (admins, stewards, staff), and 409 'Run Funder Match first' when the funder is absent from the org's latest saved run. match_for reads only the latest run's row with its full detail, so a proposal always rests on a stored match judgement.

Proposal step 1 is derived from the saved match detail by the pure gates.build: requirements for 12A, 80G, audited accounts and (for Section 135 or corporate CSR funders) CSR Form 1, with on-record text from the eligibility criterion and not_judged; CSR Form 1 is hard so a No stops the step (steps.exit_check reports it as needed by the funder); each funder's-own-bar line becomes an unchecked free-text requirement clipped to 240 characters; earlier_phase is true when the relationship criterion earned points.

new_work (in api/routes/proposals.py) stores in a new proposal at stage 1 the requirements and their cites, an empty gates map, earlier_phase, the match id/score/run_at, the funder's newest proposal_template document if any (found by repositories/proposals.funder_form), and a default style; create_proposal inserts it through repositories/proposals.create with an initial readiness summary. The proposal keeps this snapshot, so a later Funder Match rerun does not change it, and the list's fit_score reads the stored match score from work.match.

Migration 0048 aligns the proposals insert and update RLS policies with the Funder Match run rule (app.my_match_org_ids() or staff), so members read proposals but cannot start or write them; the proposals table now has work and summary jsonb columns and a server backend, so proposals are no longer browser-only.

build_agent (ask/agent.py) adds a CompareFitBudget middleware to the Ask stack that refuses, in code, a compare_fit call repeating the same org_id and sorted funder_ids earlier in the current turn, or any call beyond MAX_COMPARE_FIT_CALLS (3) per question, returning an error ToolMessage without running the tool; different funder_ids are a distinct call and a new human message resets the count.
The COMING_SOON set in the Ask frontend is currently empty, so the Funder Match card's Start a proposal action and the proposal-status filter are live rather than disabled with a Coming soon tag.

The /scores API (api/routes/scores.py, repositories/scores.py) is a separate store from match-v2 saved runs: it serves the older fit_scores/fit_score_items/rubrics/score_adjustments tables. GET /scores returns a paged envelope filtered by org/funder (slug or id) and rubric version, ordered by rubric version, total_score desc, id, and rejects an oversized limit with 422; GET /scores/{id} returns the score with per-criterion items and the adjustment log (404 if unknown). Nothing in backend/app/matching/ reads or writes these tables.

POST /scores/{id}/adjustments records a manual score adjustment as an audit row stamped with the signed-in user (require_user) as adjusted_by, returns 201, 404 when the fit score does not exist and 422 on an empty reason; it does not modify fit_scores totals or item scores, and RLS (score_adjustments_insert) allows it only for scores of orgs the caller may write to, or staff.

frontend funder-match/api.ts is a thin wrapper over the shared call helper exposing getMatches (GET /api/funder-matches?org=, URL-encoded), getDetail (GET /api/funder-matches/{id}/detail), runMatch (POST /api/funder-matches/runs?org=) and the RunSummary type; run permission is enforced by the backend, and the MatchCard tests verify the detail is fetched once from the detail URL and that starting a proposal opens it.
